name: One application is one record: reconcile a saved applicant by job and applicationId
request: One application is one record: reconcile a saved applicant by job and applicationId
checks: npm run check passed (typecheck, build, 424 tests, validate)
result: Prerequisite for the list pass, and a latent duplicate bug in its own right. applicantId hashes jobId|profileUrl|name|applicationId, so HOW MUCH OF A PERSON WAS KNOWN when they were written decides their key: a pass that reads only the list row knows the job, the application and the name but no profile URL, while a pass that opens the panel knows all four. Same person, same application, two hashes, two stored records - and silently, because saveApplicant only ever looked up incoming.id. Schema v6 adds ONE index and nothing else: applicants.applicationId. saveApplicant now consults findStoredApplication(incoming) when the id lookup misses, scoped to the job because the index is on the application id alone and an applicant is a person on a job; mergeApplicantRecord already keeps id: before.id, so the found record keeps the key it is stored under and nothing is re-keyed or deleted. The index is created against the store AS IT ALREADY EXISTS rather than inside the create-the-store branch - every user who has collected an applicant is on v5 with that store already there, so the other placement would never reach any of them - and a database still on v5 answers 'nothing stored' rather than throwing on every single save. Additive only: nothing dropped, no field removed, so a rollback to v5 costs this lookup and not one applicant, profile or queue row. Rule 14 amended to state the index, the reason and the placement.
